role: bounded source-author EDTA identity options; no authority promotion
query: select subject,predicate,value from statements where predicate in ('rdfs:label','oio:hasExactSynonym','oio:hasRelatedSynonym','oio:hasBroadSynonym','oio:hasNarrowSynonym') and (lower(value) like '%edta%' or lower(value) like '%edetate%' or lower(value) like '%edetic%' or lower(value) like '%ethylenediaminetetraacet%' or lower(value) like '%ethylenedinitrilotetraacet%') order by subject,predicate,value

properties: An organic calcium salt that is the monocalcium salt of ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA).
A magnesium salt that is the monomagnesium salt of ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA).
A tetracarboxylic acid anion formed by deprotonation of all four carboxy groups in ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA).
A tetracarboxylic acid that is chiral and consists of EDTA having a 4-[N'-(2-hydroxyethyl)thioureido]benzyl substituent at the 2-position.
An organic calcium salt of EDTA diisodium. It is a chelating agent that is used for the treatment of lead poisoning.
A tetracarboxylic acid consisting of ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid having a 4-bromoacetamidobenzyl group at the C1-position and (S)-configuration.

A combined intercalating and chelating reagent. The iron chelate, prepared by adding Fe(NH4)2(SO4)2, effects random oxidative cleavage of DNA in the presence of O2 and a reducing agent. This activity is useful as a footprinting probe.
The organic sodium salt of ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) in which three sodium cations are associated with one trianion of EDTA.
A tetracarboxylic acid anion formed by deprotonation of three of the four carboxy groups in ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA).
An organic sodium salt that is the anhydrous form of the disodium salt of ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA).
A tetracarboxylic acid anion formed by deprotonation of two of the four carboxy groups in ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA).
A hydrate that is the dihydrate form of EDTA disodium salt.

An iron chelate resulting from the deprotonation of all four carboxy groups of ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid and the addition of an iron(3+) and a sodium ion. It is used for the treatment of iron deficiency anaemia.

search_scope: All label and synonym statements in this pinned ChEBI SQLite graph, plus four fresh issuing entities. This is a bounded ontology query, not a whole-internet absence claim. Hidden/ignored filesystem filtering does not affect a direct full-database SQL scan.
result: No matching EDTA-specific term inspected here denotes an explicit union of all acid/salt/protonation forms. CHEBI:4735 is a genuine named neutral parent acid and EDTA synonym carrier; it must not be described as a charge-agnostic class. Its broad is-a ancestors include other chemical skeletons or functional groups and cannot carry an EDTA-specific assay effect without overgeneralization.

conditional_patch.status: Root selected this explicit canonical named-parent normalization proposal; independent science review must judge it. Never interpret it as a form-specific measured neutral-acid effect.

root_requested_normalization_proposal.subject: CHEBI:4735
root_requested_normalization_proposal.append_to_edge_description: The source names EDTA without a salt or protonation specification. CHEBI:4735 is used only as the named parent-acid reference for that reagent; this normalization does not establish addition of the neutral acid, a sodium salt, or a unique solution microspecies.

required_scope: Retain the observed EDTA inhibition and exact conditions whether or not the conditional graph normalization is accepted. The chemical identity gap is narrower than the mechanism evidence gap, which is resolved.
